answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each agent to post a refundable stake bond tied to one verified hardware-backed identity before it can trade. Like a lotus rooted in one pond, an identity cannot wander across many accounts without paying again for each. A bad act slashes the bond, and the loss ripples through the attacker's whole portfolio, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs thousands of bonds — far more than any single fraud gains.
